subject: psychology
topicDisplay: HL Extension: Data Analysis and Interpretation
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is a measure of central tendency?
questions.explain: Mean, median and mode measure central tendency; range and SD measure dispersion.

questions.q: The standard deviation is a measure of:
questions.explain: The SD summarises spread around the mean.

questions.q: When data are skewed or contain outliers, the more robust average is the:
questions.explain: The median is less affected by extreme values than the mean.

questions.q: Saying a result is 'statistically significant' (p < 0.05) means it is:
options: Unlikely to have occurred by chance alone
questions.explain: Significance indicates the result is unlikely under chance; it is not proof of importance or causation.

questions.q: A correlation coefficient (r) can range from:
questions.explain: r indicates strength and direction of a linear relationship, from −1 to +1.

questions.q: Why is 'statistically significant' not the same as 'important'?
options: A tiny effect can be significant in a large sample, so effect size matters
Significance always means a large effect
Importance is measured by the mode
Significance applies only to qualitative data
questions.explain: Large samples can make trivial effects significant; effect size and relevance also matter.

questions.q: A study reports r = 0.6. The best interpretation is that the variables are:
options: Moderately positively related, but causation is not established
questions.explain: A positive coefficient shows a moderate positive association; correlation is not causation.

questions.q: Thematic analysis is a method for:
options: Identifying patterns (themes) in qualitative data through coding
questions.explain: It codes qualitative data to identify recurring themes.

questions.q: In qualitative research, 'credibility' broadly parallels which quantitative idea?
questions.explain: Credibility is part of trustworthiness and parallels internal validity.

questions.q: Reflexivity in qualitative analysis means the researcher:
options: Reflects on how their own assumptions shape interpretation
questions.explain: Reflexivity makes the researcher's influence explicit, supporting trustworthiness.

questions.q: Trustworthiness criteria in qualitative research include credibility, transferability, dependability and:
questions.explain: The four trustworthiness criteria are credibility, transferability, dependability and confirmability.

questions.q: To strengthen the credibility of qualitative findings, a researcher could use:
options: Triangulation across methods or data sources
A single coder with no checks

questions.q: Matching claim to design, an experiment (not a correlation) is needed to support a claim about:
questions.explain: Only experiments with manipulation and control can support causal claims.

questions.q: Good conclusions should always be reported alongside:
questions.explain: Stating limitations (sampling, bias, generalisability) is part of honest interpretation.

questions.q: A large study finds a statistically significant but tiny difference between groups. A responsible conclusion notes that:
options: The effect may be too small to matter in practice
The effect must be very important
questions.explain: Significance with a tiny effect size may lack practical importance.

questions.q: Interpreting data honestly, without over-claiming, reflects which key concept?
questions.explain: Responsibility includes the ethical duty to interpret and report findings honestly.
The mode is the most frequent value; the range measures spread; the mean/median/mode are central tendency.

questions.q: A key reason to distinguish significance from effect size is that:
options: Significance depends partly on sample size, effect size does not
questions.explain: With large samples, small effects can be significant, so effect size gives a fuller picture.
